newsitem.title: UK: Dollar steady after German M3, awaits French audit.
newsitem.headline: Dollar steady after German M3, awaits French audit.

text.p: The dollar edged above 1.79 marks in morning Europe in cautious trade ahead of the release of France's public finances audit later this morning.

Dollar/mark showed little reaction to the drop in German M3 money supply growth for June which came in at an annualised 6.4 percent against fourth quarter 1996 against 7.0 previously and just under the Bundesbank's target corridor of 3.5-6.5 percent.
Dollar/yen, meantime, sat in tight ranges in the mid-115 yen level with trade stifled in morning Europe by a holiday in Japan and shrugging off a fresh bout of fresh turmoil in Asian currencies.
There was little reaction to one of the French public finance auditors saying France's deficit was running between 3.5 and 3.7 percent of GDP, in line with market expectations.
French finance minister Dominiqe Strauss-Kahn is to hold a news conference on the audit and measures to be implemented by the government at around 0830 GMT.
"Most of the damage has been done in anticipation of it, the government will have prepared the market for the worst," said Tim Fox, international economist at Standard Chartered.
The 3.5-3.7 percent range will keep the EMU process alive and is likely to give little relief to recent mark weakness.
Government sources said higher corporate taxes are one of the measures to bring the deficit down to within reach of the monetary union three percent target.
Extra measures are seen taking the deficit down to 3.2-3.3 percent, a level that will be more palatable to the Germans, said analysts.
By 0810 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7914/19 marks compared with 1.7883/88 late Friday in Europe. Against the yen, it stood at 115.62/72 from 115.50/60.
There was little dollar reaction to fresh turmoil in Asian currency markets which saw fresh lows for the Indonesian rupiah.
